c.tagline: A sliver of coral where the runway doubles as Main Street.

taxi.color: No official taxi fleet; unmarked private cars
taxi.fareNote: There are no metered taxis; a small number of private cars and pickup trucks give informal, negotiated flat-fare rides, usually arranged through guesthouses.

emergency.note: Medical facilities are very basic; serious cases require medical evacuation to Fiji or Australia/New Zealand, so travel insurance with medevac cover is strongly advised.

hood_desc: The commercial and administrative core of the atoll, wrapped around the airport runway, main wharf and government offices; best for travelers who want to be steps from arrivals and departures.
A busy central village around the Tuvalu Co-operative Society store and market stalls; suits travelers who want easy access to shops, banks and eateries.
Home to Princess Margaret Hospital and several government ministries, a slightly quieter stretch just off the runway; good for longer-stay visitors, officials and aid workers.
The atoll's most populous village, a mix of family compounds and small guesthouses along the lagoon side; suits travelers wanting an everyday residential feel.
A laid-back northern village known for church life and lagoon views, popular with visitors seeking a quieter pace away from the airport bustle.

water.note: Water comes from rainwater catchment and wells with contamination risk; use bottled or boiled water.

sys.n: Informal shared pickup trucks/vans (no fixed routes or schedule)

transit.pay: There is no ticketed public transit system; informal shared trucks and private vehicles are paid in cash with a negotiated flat fare, and most residents and visitors get around on foot, bicycle, or rented motorbike along the single main road.
transit.hours: No fixed schedule; informal transport and errands mostly happen during daylight hours (roughly 6am-9pm).
transit.note: Funafuti's entire road network is a single road of about 10 km running the length of Fongafale islet, so walking, cycling, and motorbike rental (about $10/day) are the main ways to get around.

transit.m: Walk to Vaiaku town centre (5-10 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not part of local custom in Tuvalu and is not expected in restaurants, guesthouses, or for other services.
